name: WalkScape
tagline: A fitness MMORPG where your real-world steps power the grinding, crafting, and leveling.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Long-running open beta with a supporter/cosmetic model, so treat any number as unknown until checked.

verdictSummary: The technical core here is genuinely trivial: read a step counter, convert steps into ticks, apply ticks to a skill, save to disk. An agent will hand you that in an afternoon and it will even be mildly satisfying for about two days. What it cannot hand you is several thousand hours of designed content: skill trees that interlock, recipes worth chasing, drop tables tuned so the next thing is always almost in reach, zones that gate on gear you do not have yet. Add clubs, a player market, and the specific knowledge that other people are walking the same grind, and you are no longer building software, you are building a game. A solo save file with no content pipeline is a step counter wearing a hat.
coreLoopDIY: A local mobile app that turns your daily step count into idle progression across a handful of hand-written skills, with offline catch-up and no server.
requirements: An iOS or Android device with a working pedometer
Expo dev build plus health/motion permissions (Apple Health or Google Fit fallback for backfill)
You writing the actual content: skills, recipes, drop tables, item art or emoji stand-ins
Acceptance that everything lives in one local database with no cloud sync
whatYouLose: The content: hundreds of hours of interlocking skills, recipes, zones, and drops you would have to design yourself
Other players entirely: clubs, leaderboards, the market, and the social pressure that makes a step grind stick
Balance and tuning, which is the actual craft here and cannot be one-shotted
Cross-device sync, cheat resistance, and anti-tamper on step data
Ongoing updates, so your version is permanently finished on day two
moatNotes: The moat is a content pipeline plus a live playerbase, which is the least clonable pair in software.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because the grind is designed to be worth doing and because other people are doing it. A self-built version gives you a number that goes up when you walk, which your phone already does for free. The value was never the pedometer read, it was somebody else deciding what the steps unlock and keeping that list growing for years.
notes: A step-fed idle loop is a weekend build; a game world is not. The moat is years of designed content plus the clubs and player market full of people already grinding it.
prompt:
Build a local-only step-powered idle RPG for my own phone. This is a consolation build, not a clone.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Expo (React Native, TypeScript), expo-router for navigation
- expo-sensors Pedometer for live steps, plus a health backfill query on app open for steps taken while the app was closed
- expo-sqlite for all state, accessed through a tiny data layer in src/db.ts
- Zustand for UI state, no Redux
- No backend, no accounts, no analytics, no telemetry, no network calls at all

Game model, keep it small and readable:
- 100 steps = 1 tick. Ticks are the only currency of progress.
- Four skills defined in a single src/content/skills.ts file as plain data: Walking, Foraging, Crafting, Fishing. Each has XP curve, level cap 50, and 3 to 5 activities.
- An activity consumes N ticks per completion and yields XP plus an item roll from a weighted drop table.
- Exactly one activity is active at a time. Switching is instant and loses nothing.
- On app open: compute steps since last save, convert to ticks, resolve the active activity in a loop, and show a single "while you were away" summary modal.
- Inventory table with stack counts. Crafting recipes consume items and produce items. Recipes also live in src/content.

Screens: Home (active activity, tick balance, progress bar), Skills (list with levels and XP bars), Inventory (grid, tap for detail), Activity picker.

Explicitly out of scope: multiplayer, clubs, chat, leaderboards, trading, cloud sync, combat, maps, cosmetics, monetization, push notifications.

Requirements:
- All tunable numbers (tick cost, XP curves, drop weights) in src/content/*.ts with comments so I can rebalance without touching logic.
- Idempotent offline catch-up: never double-count steps if the app resumes twice.
- A dev-only "add 1000 steps" button behind an __DEV__ check.
- Seed the DB on first launch, then a README covering how to run it on a real device (Expo dev build, motion and health permissions) and how to add a new skill in under ten lines.
